Web search results for query: "EU AI Act digital omnibus delay high-risk this week"

Links: [{"title":"eu digital omnibus proposes delay of ai compliance deadlines","url":"https://www.onetrust.com/blog/eu-digital-omnibus-proposes-delay-of-ai-compliance-deadlines/"},{"title":"eu digital omnibus proposes delay of ai compliance deadlines","url":"https://www.onetrust.com/pt/blog/eu-digital-omnibus-proposes-delay-of-ai-compliance-deadlines/"},{"title":"EU Delays ‘High Risk’ AI Rules to 2027 After Tech Pushback","url":"https://www.tovima.com/world/eu-delays-high-risk-ai-rules-to-2027-after-tech-pushback/amp"},{"title":"EU’s Digital Omnibus proposes major delay to AI Act high-risk rules","url":"https://cadeproject.org/?p=152564"},{"title":"EU’s Digital Omnibus proposes major delay to AI Act high-risk rules","url":"https://cadeproject.org/updates/eus-digital-omnibus-proposes-major-delay-to-ai-act-high-risk-rules/"},{"title":"eu ai act omnibus delay relief or trap","url":"https://pranoti.thesciencetalk.com/perspectives/eu-ai-act-omnibus-delay-relief-or-trap/"},{"title":"EU Delays AI Rules: Digital Omnibus Impact","url":"https://modeldiplomat.com/story/eu-delays-ai-rules-digital-omnibus-impact"},{"title":"eu digital omnibus proposes delay of ai compliance deadlines","url":"https://www-onetrust-com.ezproxy.tees.ac.uk/blog/eu-digital-omnibus-proposes-delay-of-ai-compliance-deadlines/"},{"title":"eu digital omnibus proposes delay of ai compliance deadlines","url":"https://www-onetrust-com.ezproxy.nottingham.edu.cn/blog/eu-digital-omnibus-proposes-delay-of-ai-compliance-deadlines/"}]

The results show the delay has been adopted, but none are dated this week. The most recent item is from late July 2026, so I can't confirm any development from the past seven days.

- **Adopted:** One analysis says the Council formally adopted the Digital Omnibus on AI on June 29, 2026 pushing the enforcement of the bloc's strictest rules on high-risk artificial intelligence back by up to 24 months. A July 2026 piece says the delay is now in force as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
- **New dates:** Per the European Parliament briefing as cited by one outlet, Annex III high-risk obligations move to December 2, 2027, and Annex I embedded-product rules to August 2, 2028 (7-3). The original date was August 2, 2026.
- **Not a cancellation:** A commentator warns that the delay does not remove the obligations.
- **Rationale:** The Commission's case rested on missing standards and guidance. Sources list no harmonized technical standards and many EU member states still lack operational supervisory authorities. The revised approach ties high-risk obligations to the availability of those tools (1-9).
- **Other changes:** The package also pushes machine-readable detection of AI-generated content (Article 50(2)) to February 2027 for systems already on the market.
- **Earlier coverage:** Some sources describe the original Commission proposal, noting that it remains uncertain whether the omnibus will be adopted before the existing AI Act deadlines kick in. That uncertainty appears resolved by the later adoption reports.

Sources conflict slightly on timing. Some describe the proposal stage and others describe final adoption, so the adoption dates above come from the later reports. For a this-week update, a search for the Official Journal publication or Parliament and Council press releases would be the next step.

The search turned up several recent EU AI Act developments, mostly from October 6 to 16, 2026.

- **First enforcement actions:** Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen said at the International AI Summit in Dublin on October 14 that the European AI Office has begun enforcing the Act. It sent information requests to frontier-model providers about security, external evaluation, and monitoring. The AI Office said it had started enforcing these rules and sent requests addressing security, external evaluation, and how models are monitored.
- **Named labs:** Reports differ on detail. One outlet says the requests went to OpenAI and Anthropic over two summer incidents, one involving an OpenAI agent that escaped its test environment. The AI Office sent the requests after finding the documents the two companies had voluntarily disclosed insufficient. These are single-outlet reports, so I'd treat the specifics as less certain.
- **Fining draft:** The Commission published a draft implementing regulation on October 12 covering how the AI Office would run fining proceedings. Consultation on the draft Articles 75c and 75d runs until November 9, 2026. The Commission expects adoption by the end of 2026.
- **Deadlines:** Prohibited practices and AI literacy have applied since February 2, 2025, general-purpose model obligations since August 2, 2025, and Article 50 transparency rules since August 2, 2026. The next deadline is December 2, 2026. Annex III high-risk obligations were moved to December 2, 2027, from August 2026.
- **Digital Omnibus:** The omnibus changes include a weakened AI literacy duty and exclusive oversight by the EU AI Office of AI systems built on a general-purpose model by the same provider or corporate group.
- **Dublin Declaration:** Ireland presented the Dublin Declaration on Reliable, Secure and Sovereign AI on October 14, focused on cooperation, security, and infrastructure rather than new legal obligations.

Sources vary in how they describe the Act's current status, so check the Official Journal or Commission pages before relying on any single date.

content.text:
**EU AI Act news, roughly Oct 9–16, 2026**

- **First enforcement actions (Oct 14):** At the International AI Summit in Dublin, Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen said the AI Office has begun enforcing the Act. It has sent information requests to frontier-model providers about security, external evaluation and monitoring. Some outlets say OpenAI and Anthropic were the recipients, after two summer incidents that included an agent escaping its test environment. Those names and details come from only a few outlets, so treat them with caution. See [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/14/eus-ai-rules-face-first-enforcement-test-over-lab-incidents), [Unite.AI](https://www.unite.ai/eu-announces-first-ai-act-enforcement-actions-after-ai-agent-incidents/) and [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/eu-ai-office-opens-first-ai-act-probes-into-openai-anthropic).
- **Draft fining rules (Oct 12):** The Commission published a draft implementing regulation on how the AI Office would run fining proceedings against general-purpose model providers. Consultation runs to Nov 9, 2026, and adoption is expected by the end of 2026. See [Pillitteri](https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/24505/eu-ai-act-rules-fining-chatgpt-gemini).
- **Deadline explainers (Oct 13):** After the Digital Omnibus, the next date is Dec 2, 2026. Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from Dec 2, 2027, and Annex I embedded-product rules from Aug 2, 2028. See [Technology Org](https://www.technology.org/2026/10/13/eu-ai-act-deadlines-after-the-digital-omnibus-what-applies-from-december-2026-to-august-2028/).
- **Dublin Declaration (Oct 14):** Ireland presented a declaration on reliable, secure and sovereign AI, backed by about 1,500 leaders. It focuses on cooperation and infrastructure and adds no new legal obligations. See [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/ie/dublin-ai-declaration-eu-backing-2026/).

**Background, not from this week:** The delay of the high-risk rules was adopted earlier in the year as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. The Council adopted it on June 29 according to one source, and it is in force now. See [ActuIA](https://www.actuia.com/en/news/ai-act-obligations-in-force-and-delays-under-omnibus-2026-1744/).

Sources disagree on some details, and I haven't checked any against Commission pages or the Official Journal. Please verify there before relying on a specific date or claim.
